newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cost-cutting plan to net 6.5 bln reais.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cost-cutting plan to net 6.5 bln reais.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said Friday a package of cost-cutting measures would deliver a net gain to the government of 6.5 billion reais in 1997.

Malan, announcing a series of federal cost-cutting and revenue-raising measures at a news conference, said he expected the public sector operational deficit to be 3.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1996.
The finance minister said there would be further gains in terms of the federal government's finances in 1997 through measures to cut outlays in the next budget.

The public sector operational deficit stood at 3.72 percent of GDP in the first seven months compared with Malan's projection at the beginning of the year that the 1996 deficit would be half of last year's 5.0 percent of GDP.
The package of measures announced Friday is intended to show Brasilia can tackle the deficit without depending on the passage of key fiscal reforms through a recalcitrant Congress.
